feedback: Earlier evidence (iteration 0, 60 trials, 0 finishes on any track): every run ended off track. Progress was 0.11 to 0.17, max_error was 0.061 to 0.066 against an off-track limit of about 0.0575 m for this body width, and rms_error stayed low at 0.03 to 0.034. The robot drifts outward steadily rather than oscillating, so speed and steady offset are the main suspects, not jitter. This candidate addresses that directly: base_speed 1.6 to 1.2, ki 0 to 0.2 to cancel the constant motor mismatch, kp 3 to 4 and kd 0.2 to 0.6 for a stronger, damped correction, and sensors moved to y = 0.05 with x spread to ±0.03 so they see the line earlier and across wider bends. Body width stays at the maximum (0.18 m) for the widest off-track allowance. All values are inside the contract ranges and the wheel command stays within limits. Nothing here is obviously broken. Because the baseline never survived a run, surviving the full course is worth far more than finish time (surviving at progress 1 scores roughly 390 even without completion, against about 50 for the baseline). The change is the right direction on the evidence, so approve it and race it now. It also changes several fields at once, so the next race should be read carefully to tell which change did what. Conditional follow-ups for after the race: (a) if it survives but completion_time is above 3 s, raise base_speed in steps of 0.1 (1.3, then 1.4) while watching max_error, since completion needs roughly 1.5 m/s average; (b) if steering_oscillation rises sharply or max_error grows on the s-bend and slalom, reduce kp to about 3 and keep kd at 0.6; (c) if line_loss_events stays above 0, widen sensor x spread (for example ±0.04 at sensor_size 0.012) before changing gains.
requested_changes: If the candidate survives but completion_time exceeds 3 s with low max_error: raise base_speed in 0.1 steps (1.3, then 1.4), keeping the other fields fixed, because iteration 0 showed off-track failures at speed 1.6 and the 1.2 setting is the first survival attempt.

If steering_oscillation rises sharply or max_error grows on the s-bend and slalom: reduce kp from 4.0 to about 3.0 and keep kd at 0.6, since the baseline's kp 3 with kd 0.2 showed no oscillation problem but the stronger gain is untested.

If line_loss_events stays above 0 with the new forward sensors: widen the sensor x spread from ±0.03 to about ±0.04 at sensor_size 0.012, because the baseline showed 1 to 2 line-loss events per run on sharp bends.
